title: One organic reel, 100+ paid sign-ups | MANA
description: Kevin Chiang's organic reel for Suapp did 490K+ views, 29K saves and 100+ paid sign-ups, with no boost and no whitelisting. What made the match work.
h1: Case study: one organic reel, 100+ paid sign-ups for Suapp
lede: One organic Instagram reel by Kevin Chiang for Suapp, a SketchUp plug-in, reached 490K+ views, 29K saves and 100+ paid sign-ups. There was no paid boost and no whitelisting behind it.

body: Suapp makes a plug-in for SketchUp. Kevin Chiang (@kevnchiang) is an architecture and design creator in Melbourne, managed by MANA, and he showed the plug-in inside his own content rather than in a product demo.
The reel did 490K+ views, 17K likes, 29K saves and 12K comments. Suapp recorded 100+ paid sign-ups from that one post. No boost, no whitelisting, no ad spend behind it.

sections.h2: Why does a 14K-follower account reach 490,000 people?
body: Because reach on Reels is not the same thing as follower count. 92% of Kevin's reach is non-follower. Across a 30-day window his account does 928K+ views, 359K unique viewers and 40K average reel views.
So the follower number is the wrong thing to brief against. The Suapp reel landed well above his 40K average, and nearly all of that reach came from people who had never followed him.

sections.h2: Why were saves the number to watch?
body: This reel got 29K saves against 17K likes. A like is a reaction to a video. A save on a software reel is closer to intent: someone has parked a tool to install the next time they open their laptop.
If you are selling a product that a viewer has to go and set up, saves and comments tell you more about pipeline than likes do. On this post there were 12K comments as well.

The product and the audience were the same people. Kevin's lane is architecture and design, and 88% of his audience is aged 18 to 34, split evenly between men and women. Their stated interests include architecture, student life, tech, fashion, health and running.

His top markets by followers are India at 12.1%, Australia at 9.2% and the USA at 6.9%, with Melbourne the single biggest city at 6.2%. That is a software buyer base for a SketchUp plug-in: students and young architects who already have the host program open.
He has run 45+ brand partnerships across design, tech and lifestyle, so the plug-in demo sat in a format his audience was used to seeing from him.
The same pattern shows up at a smaller size. His reel "5 tools you should know as an architecture student" did 161K views, 5.4K likes and 11K saves, and produced 25 sign-ups on a mobile app.
Smaller reach, same mechanism: a tool shown to people who were already looking for tools.

sections.h2: What has to be true for a sign-up campaign to work?
body: Nothing here is a promise of the same outcome. It is a checklist of the conditions that were in place when it worked.
bullets: The product can be tried the same day, with no sales call in the way.
There is a short path from reel to sign-up: a free tier, a trial, or a single landing page.
Tracking is live before the post is: a code, a tagged link or a dedicated page.
The creator already works in your category, so the product is not a surprise to the audience.
The brief sets the problem and the proof points, and the creator chooses the format.
Usage rights and dates are agreed in writing before filming, in case you want to run the footage as an ad later.
You and the creator agree up front how long you will measure for.

sections.h2: Where do these campaigns usually go wrong?
body: A common way it goes wrong is the brand writing the script. The reel turns into a feature list, the audience scrolls, and the post gets blamed on reach.
Another common one is attribution. The link changes the week after the post goes up, so nobody can tell which sign-ups came from where, and a working campaign looks flat in the report.
MANA handles that side for its creators: scope, deliverables, usage and dates in writing, and one point of contact from the first brief to the final post.

faq: Was there any paid media behind the Suapp reel?
No. The 490K+ views were organic, with no boost and no whitelisting. Partnership ads and whitelisting are separate options, and neither was used on this post.
Can you really attribute paid sign-ups to one reel?

Suapp counted 100+ paid sign-ups from it. That only works when a tracked link, code or dedicated landing page is in place before the reel goes live, which is why tracking belongs in the brief and not in the post-mortem.
What kinds of products suit Kevin Chiang's audience?

Things architecture students and young designers use: design and rendering software, plug-ins, hardware and tools. 88% of his audience is aged 18 to 34, his top markets are India, Australia and the USA, and Melbourne is his biggest city. Ask MANA for his media kit to see the full audience data.
